source.title: A Unified Scaling Law for Time Series Foundation Models
source.authors: Xilin Dai; Yi-Ding Liu; Ze-Wei Dong; Jiang-Nan Yang; Qiang Xu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present through Appendix E.5; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling behavior in the new setting of pretrained time-series foundation models, using forecasting MASE rather than language-model pretraining cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own capacity/context scaling law and held-out prediction results. Its matched-history, rule-retention, and activation-patching experiments concern other learning hypotheses and are not rows for these claim versions. Earlier scaling results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits and validates a capacity–context–horizon law for frozen time-series foundation models (normalized forecasting MASE). That is a new modality with its own result on capacity scaling (V5) and on how predictably forecasting performance tracks scale (V6). Capacity comes from heterogeneous released checkpoints, not a controlled sweep of N, tokens or compute.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that a five-parameter law fits average TSFM capacity, context and horizon returns. They say it predicts Public results and held-out Toto 2.0 capacity curves, and they present it as empirical support for pretraining larger models and as a reusable methodology. They do not foreground that a capacity-free form predicts about as well.
record.recipe_differences: Uses heterogeneous released TSFM checkpoints and controlled forecasting evaluations, fitting normalized MASE as a function of active parameters, input length, and forecast horizon. It does not sweep language-model training tokens or compute or measure held-out language-model cross-entropy.
record.method_sensitivity: Capacity gains depend on input length in the fitted law. On a fixed complete-support subset, context gains become slightly negative beyond 4096; fitted saturation scales are approximately 3.6k–4.6k over 10M–1B parameters (Appendix C.3).

fits_no_version.finding: Forecasting error falls with input (context) length but saturates near 3.6k–4.6k steps. Gains turn slightly negative beyond 4096 on complete support, and the saturation scale grows with capacity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For frozen TSFMs, returns to inference-time context length diminish toward a capacity-dependent saturation scale.

record.problems: The capacity/context law is estimated from heterogeneous released checkpoints rather than a controlled training sweep over model size, tokens, and compute. Coverage is uneven: only nine of 21 checkpoint interfaces support the full input grid, and the fixed complete-support analysis covers eight checkpoints and 12 tasks. Forecasting MASE is not held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were omitted. Other experiments on matched-history forecasting, adaptation, rule identification, parameter exchange, and activation interventions address learning mechanisms rather than the listed scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: Language-model held-out pretraining cross-entropy versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation of LM pretraining-loss power laws to runs orders of magnitude larger. The Toto hold-out extrapolates only ~5x in N, on forecasting MASE.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation; no training-compute or token sweep.
Depth/width or other shape changes at fixed parameter count.
Image/video, repeated data, fine-tuning/transfer scaling. Also time-series scaling in training tokens or compute, and capacity scaling with data and compute held fixed.
Downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss; downstream task families other than forecasting.
Dependence of LM exponents or compute-optimal split on counting, schedule, data or fitting method.

missing.what: Reference predictors: constant 14.83/16.92/17.10% and capacity-independent (β=0) 9.96/13.01/11.84% MAPE (Controlled/Public/Toto) vs Unified 10.13/12.82/11.53%. Paired MAPE-difference intervals include zero.
Bootstrap 95% interval for capacity–history coupling β: [0.00090, 0.00322], excluding zero.
All-checkpoint fit on Toto points: 10.4% MAPE (vs 11.5% leave-Toto-out).

record.verdict_notes: The record's labels overstate support. R2 is in-sample fit, and R2–R4 measure the joint law's accuracy, which Table 5 shows does not depend measurably on the capacity term. Capacity scaling is inferred from heterogeneous released checkpoints, so N is confounded with data, compute and architecture. Only Toto 2.0 is a clean size series.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation of language-model pretraining-loss power laws from small runs to much larger runs.
Compute-budget-optimal parameter/token allocation and its scaling with training compute.
Controlled tests of depth, width, or other architecture changes at fixed parameter count.
Tests pretrained time-series forecasters, but not image or video models, repeated-data training, or fine-tuning/transfer scaling laws; it does not test training-token or compute scaling.
Tests forecast performance against model capacity, not downstream performance as a function of language-model pretraining loss or other downstream task families.
Does not test how language-model exponents or compute-optimal allocations vary with counting, training schedule, data, or fitting choices.

rows.subject: 21 controlled TSFM checkpoints (aggregate response)
rows.operation_detail: Fits a five-parameter response law to capacity, input-length, and forecast-horizon relations.
rows.baseline: Seasonal Naive normalization; R is raw MASE divided by matched Seasonal Naive MASE.
rows.note: At fixed input length, the equation gives a capacity power-law term whose exponent depends on input length. The joint law also includes a quadratic in log input length, rather than reporting the same parameters/tokens/compute power-law form as the language-model claim.
rows.check: State is right but the note should give magnitudes. At fixed L the capacity exponent is −0.001846·log L, about −0.014 at L=2048: roughly 3% lower error per tenfold N. N is confounded with architecture, data and compute across heterogeneous checkpoints, and tokens and compute are not varied.

rows.subject: 21 controlled TSFM checkpoints (aggregate response)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluates the fitted law on the same Controlled response points used to characterize the resource relation.
rows.measure: Mean absolute percentage error of law predictions
rows.baseline: Observed response points; reference prediction comparisons are reported in Table 5.
rows.note: This is a fitted-sample prediction result, not an independent language-model loss extrapolation.
rows.check: This is in-sample fit error on the fitting points, not prediction. It scores the joint N–L–H law. A capacity-independent form (β=0) fits equally well or better (9.96% vs 10.13%, Table 5), so the row cannot show a capacity effect.

rows.subject: 22 GIFT Public TSFM checkpoints (aggregate response)
rows.operation_detail: Applies the fitted law to non-overlapping public benchmark results from a different source.
rows.measure: Mean absolute percentage error of law predictions
rows.note: The paper describes this as prediction under a different source of model results and horizon-context conditions.
rows.check: The law predicts cross-source Public points (12.82%), but the capacity-independent form gets 13.01%, and the paired MAPE-difference intervals include zero. Predictability comes mainly from context and horizon terms, not scale. Not a V5 power-law measure.

rows.subject: Toto 2.0 series (five checkpoints; aggregate response)
rows.size_stated: Approximately 4M–2.5B parameters; Table 4 gives active counts from 4.14M to 2454.28M.
rows.operation_detail: Withholds all five Toto 2.0 checkpoints, refits on the remaining heterogeneous checkpoints, and predicts Toto responses.

conditions.value: 16 heterogeneous checkpoints; all five Toto 2.0 checkpoints excluded

rows.measure: Mean absolute percentage error of predicted responses
rows.check: Held-out Toto pointwise MAPE is 11.53% vs 11.84% for the capacity-independent form, a non-significant difference (Table 5). Not a V5 power-law measure. The 1B and 2.5B Toto points also lie beyond the ~500M maximum N of the 16 fitting checkpoints.

relationships.condition: Toto 2.0 same-architecture series (4M–2.5B), horizon-averaged capacity curves at L=2048 and 4096, law fitted without Toto
relationships.reason: Capacity curves follow the fitted log-linear-in-N relation with 1.09% and 1.50% MAPE (R5, R6).
relationships.display_finding: Capacity predictions from the log-linear parameter relation achieve MAPE of 1.09% and 1.50% at context lengths 2048 and 4096, respectively.

source_check.reason: At fixed context and horizon, the fitted law is a power law in capacity. Section 5.3 reports held-out capacity-curve MAPEs of 1.09% and 1.50%, matching R5 and R6.

relationships.condition: Joint capacity–context law across 21 heterogeneous TSFM checkpoints
relationships.reason: The capacity exponent is tiny (~−0.014 at L=2048) and depends on input length via a log N·log L interaction. Context enters as a quadratic in log L, not a single power law (R1).
relationships.display_finding: The capacity exponent was approximately −0.014 at context length 2048 and varied through a log-capacity–log-context interaction, while context dependence was quadratic in log length.

source_check.reason: Equation 7 contains a capacity–context interaction and quadratic log-context term, qualifying a simple joint power-law description. Fixed-context capacity scaling remains a power law; the small capacity exponent alone is not a scope limitation.

relationships.display_finding: Capacity-free and capacity-aware predictions were similar (13.01% versus 12.82%; 11.84% versus 11.53%), with paired intervals including zero.
